evidence:
This adjudication supersedes only the missing exact-image isolation measurement in my preserved rows/46.json; it does not overwrite that original report. The frozen XLSX was inspected with openpyxl in the original independent review: Quality Checks row 47 (number 46), Internal Quality Checks row 47, and relevant deterministic Dockerfile/secret/isolation rows. The internal row repeats the public separation requirement and introduces no alternate profile. I independently rehashed all 50 frozen task files and all 34 frozen rule files against manifest.json for this adjudication: zero mismatches. The candidate remains input SHA256 27f81c18259555d26b61a5a2b0f026f0360b7380bc072523513b0ad2deca9efc.

Source separation remains sound. All task-relative paths below refer to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task. environment/Dockerfile:9-15 installs only application dependencies and copies instructions/ and assets/; :17-23 creates /app with only its initial git repository and .gitkeep. I inspected every copied note and the full seed in the original review, finding no grading material or key; all 79 criterion IDs from all five judge files had zero exact-token matches in the public instruction/environment files. task.toml:2 exports only /app and /assets; :28 specifies environment_mode = "separate"; :30-35 confines the templated provider credential to verifier.env. tests/Dockerfile:43-44 copies grading material to /tests and removes group/other permissions. tests/test.sh:3,10-12 sets umask 077 and log mode 700; :104-111 launches the app with env -i and setpriv UID/GID 65534, with only PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME, PORT and DB_PATH. Its restart path repeats that environment/identity at :160-167.

I read the complete measure_isolation.py driver, raw isolation-measurement.json outputs, and both build logs instead of accepting their aggregate passed flag. The build logs export agent image sha256:975a778efe9693f72d92a37cf40e402d4d21610b5e9f32e49edd20445d6112b0 (agent-image-build-network.log:65) and verifier image sha256:46fefc505dbcabf0d6cb4e54fea8f0880acde2f7896587750af967427598977d (verifier-image-build-network.log:75). The raw report's image IDs and docker-run command IDs exactly match those exports. The runs use --network=none and exit zero. The recorded driver SHA256 independently equals the current driver bytes: 25c548a537bbe28e2d4e3cecab1e4a2cbd5e7bdf969def52db3c935e9020e7d8.

Agent inventory (isolation-measurement.json:20-50) records UID 0, exactly the seven required note/asset hashes, /app entries [.git, .gitkeep], no /tests or /solution, no RewardKit/Claude/Codex/Playwright executables at their installed locations, no RewardKit Python package, global Node packages limited to better-sqlite3/corepack/express/npm, and no provider or RewardKit environment variables. I independently compared the complete expected and observed note/asset maps, including key-set equality: 7 expected and 7 observed, all equal. This avoids the driver's weaker all-observed-entries comparison potentially overlooking a missing expected file. The source COPY/build steps account for the task-controlled files; this is not represented as an exhaustive hostile-base-image forensic scan.

Verifier inventory (isolation-measurement.json:69-86) includes exactly 15 runtime test files with the frozen bytes and a /tests directory mode of 0700. I independently computed full map equality against all frozen tests files except tests/Dockerfile and tests/.dockerignore, correctly excluded by the actual tests/.dockerignore:1-2. There are no missing or extra runtime test files. I also inspected the preserved first-inventory raw report: it uses the same two image IDs and byte-for-byte equal observation objects; its only failed aggregate check is verifier_files_match. That initial inventory incorrectly expected these excluded build inputs in /tests. Correcting the expected set agrees with Docker's actual ignore rule and does not waive an image mismatch.

Permission probe (measure_isolation.py:27-57; isolation-measurement.json:87-139): the root verifier process creates a protected dummy reward file and an app-owned writable directory, installs harmless dummy provider/model environment markers, then launches Node through the same env -i plus setpriv UID/GID/cleared-groups settings as test.sh. The child actually reports UID/GID 65534 and only the five expected application environment names. Reads of /tests/scored/functional/judge.toml and /logs/verifier/reward.json, a write to that reward path, and a read of /proc/1/environ all fail with EACCES. The reward remains exactly unchanged. The positive control writes and reads /app/qc-public-write.txt successfully, demonstrating that these denials did not merely arise from a dead probe. No real credential was used or printed. Protected parent /tests traversal and the matching recursive chmod account for the other criteria and policy files.

The plausible malicious server witness is now exercised: equivalent unprivileged Node code attempts to read criteria, forge reward output, and read the root process environment, and is denied; an ordinary conforming app still writes its working directory successfully. No false-pass or false-fail witness remains established for this row. The driver reproduces the relevant launch identity/environment and permission setup in the exact images; it does not execute all of tests/test.sh or run a model. This supplies the narrow exact-image and OS-permission evidence missing from my original row46 report. Verdict Pass / CONFIRMED applies to check46 only. A complete configured judge run, provider evaluation, Oracle score, target-model score and measured judge workload remain unmeasured and are not implied by this adjudication.
